newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the three main ideas that could be drawn from the Commission's European Economy report No4, were that due to the achievement of the internal market GDP was more than one percent higher than it would have been otherwise, the number of jobs gained could be estimated at between 300,000 and 900,000, and exchanges between member states had increased by 20 to 30 percent. He also said that at the beginning of the 90s the European Union had absorbed 44 percent of world foreign investment flow.

In answer to a question, spokesman Peter Guilford said the EU anti-dumping committee was still discussing the Commission proposal to impose provisional duties on Norwegian farmed Atlantic salmon imports. He said the committee's conclusions, which would probably be reached in the afternoon, would not be binding.

On the issue of gray cotton, Guilford said the potential definitive anti-dumping duties would be decided by the Council in a simple majority vote. He also said the member states were roughly split for and againt the continuation of duties.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/271: Information Society: the employment and local development: lauch of European Social Fund pilot projects.
- Speech/97/76: Speech by Commissioner Padraig Flynn at European round table lunch on ERT Report "A stimulus to job creation".
- Speech/97/77: Presentation by Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy of the book "EMU explained".
- Speech/97/79: Speech by Commissioner Mario Monti on the Information Society and SMEs.
- Eurostat news release No 26/97: EU annual inflation: 2.0% in February.
- European Economy No4-1996 - Reports and studies.
